text:
jen: FYI customer BrightLeaf reports missing days in their CSV usage export (they see tokens on invoice but CSV has gaps). export_job_id=exp-20260310-9f3a, S3 prefix s3://redwood-exports/brightleaf/2026-03/
marc: thanks Jen — can you paste a tiny snippet of the CSV (header + surrounding rows) and the invoice lineID they reference? :eyes:
jen: here’s the CSV excerpt they shared (they redacted user ids):\n\n```
date,customer_id,model,tokens
2026-03-09,brightleaf,redwood-rt-1,41234
2026-03-11,brightleaf,redwood-rt-1,38901
```
\nThey expected a row for 2026-03-10 but it’s absent. Invoice shows token charge for 2026-03-10: invoice_line=inv-L-7834, tokens=12012. Customer says they downloaded the CSV using dashboard -> exports -> raw usage (CSV).
li: quick hypothesis — combine_shards step in the export pipeline may have dropped an empty shard manifest during the cutover. Can you share the export manifest and job logs? I can grep for job id.
jen: pasted job log link: https://internal-logs/exp-20260310-9f3a (internal) — key lines below: \n\n```
[2026-03-10T02:15:12Z] export-service: started job exp-20260310-9f3a
[2026-03-10T02:15:45Z] export-service: generated shard list (3 shards)
[2026-03-10T02:16:01Z] combine_shards: step returned status=success, merged_files=2, expected=3
[2026-03-10T02:16:02Z] deploy-bot: marked export as COMPLETE
```
\nmarc: merged_files != expected is worrying — looks like one shard went missing but job returned success. @data-ops can you check S3 for that job path and list objects? maybe a late uploader failed but combine_shards ignored it.
billing-bot: Automated check: billing rows exist for customer=brightleaf date=2026-03-10 in billingdb.transactions (row_id=bill-20260310-001, tokens=12012). Quick dump shows provenance export_job_ref=exp-20260309-9f3a (note different job id).
sara: interesting — billing shows tokens but billing.ref points to exp-20260309-9f3a while CSV export job is exp-20260310-9f3a. Two different pipeline runs. Could be a gap introduced when we changed export cutover schedule (daily roll moved from 02:00 to 02:15 UTC) last week.
li: can someone run this query against the raw events DB to confirm rows exist for 2026-03-10? Suggest SQL: \n\n```
SELECT date(event_time) as d, count(*) as rows, sum(tokens) as tokens
FROM raw.usage_events
WHERE customer_id='brightleaf' AND date(event_time) between '2026-03-09' and '2026-03-11'
GROUP BY d
ORDER BY d;
```
\nI ran it against recent replica and got: 2026-03-09 rows=412, tokens=41234; 2026-03-10 rows=123, tokens=12012; 2026-03-11 rows=389, tokens=38901. So raw data present.
data-ops: Confirmed S3 listing for s3://redwood-exports/brightleaf/2026-03/exp-20260310-9f3a/ shows two shard files: shard-0.csv.gz, shard-1.csv.gz. shard-2.csv.gz is missing. However we have shard-2 uploaded to a different prefix: s3://redwood-exports/brightleaf/2026-03/exp-20260309-9f3a/shard-2.csv.gz. Looks like during the deployment window a retry wrote the missing shard to the previous day's job id. :facepalm:
marc: ahhhh so combine_shards for the 03/10 job ran before the last shard arrived and then marked success. We need two actions: 1) backfill the missing shard into exp-20260310-9f3a prefix and rerun combine_shards OR 2) re-run the export job for 2026-03-10 and upload a merged CSV. Which is less risky?
li: backfill is safe — just copy shard-2 from exp-20260309 prefix -> exp-20260310 prefix and re-run combine_shards for that job id. That preserves object paths customers expect (same job id in manifest). I can run a dry-run copy and then trigger combine_shards.
jen: customer asked for ETA because they already received an invoice and want CSV for reconciliation. Can we give a timeline? @sara billing needs to know if invoice lines need adjustment.
sara: invoice is correct (charges are in billingdb). We don't need to change invoice. Just provide CSV file to customer. Aim for < 3 hours. I can notify customer of temporary workaround: they can use the Usage API to pull raw rows until we restore CSV.
li: executing backfill now: cp s3://redwood-exports/brightleaf/2026-03/exp-20260309-9f3a/shard-2.csv.gz s3://redwood-exports/brightleaf/2026-03/exp-20260310-9f3a/shard-2.csv.gz && invoke combine_shards --job exp-20260310-9f3a
deploy-bot: combine_shards( exp-20260310-9f3a ) re-run queued by li at 2026-03-10T05:20:12Z
deploy-bot: combine_shards: completed, merged_files=3, output=exp-20260310-9f3a/merged.csv.gz
li: verified merged.csv.gz contains 2026-03-10 row. Ran quick checksum and spot-checked token sums. Good. I uploaded a fresh CSV to public export location: https://exports.redwood.ai/brightleaf/2026-03/exp-20260310-9f3a/merged.csv.gz
jen: replied to customer with workaround + link, cc billing. Customer confirmed they can reconcile now. :thumbsup:
marc: follow-up item — add a check in the export pipeline that fails the job if merged_files != expected or that waits for late shard arrivals for X minutes (configurable). Filed ticket: PLAT-5731 (export pipeline: enforce shard completeness). @data-ops pls prioritize.
li: also looking into why the retry wrote to previous job prefix — likely race during job id rotation in uploader. Will open a PR to namespace uploader writes by monotonic run id.\n\n---\nNotes: root cause = shard uploaded to older job prefix during cutover window; combine_shards marked success prematurely. Resolution = backfill copy + re-run combine_shards, customer CSV provided. Billing unaffected. Suggested mitigations: pipeline completeness check + uploader namespacing + alert when merged_files != expected.
